title: Erdős Problem #1145: The Erdős–Sárközy Conjecture on Two-Set Bases
description: If A, B ⊆ ℕ are infinite with aₙ/bₙ → 1 and A + B covers all large integers, must the two-set representation function r_{A,B}(n) be unbounded? Status: OPEN.

meta.assumptions: 10 axiom declarations: erdos_sarkozy_conjecture (main open conjecture), ruzsaA_infinite, ruzsaB_infinite, ruzsa_unique_rep, ruzsa_rep_bounded, ruzsa_is_basis, ruzsa_ratio_not_one (Ruzsa counterexample properties from Problem #331), sum_of_reps_bound, average_rep_grows, grekos_two_set (partial results). All 10 theorems/lemmas proved without sorry.
prerequisites: Filter convergence and limits in Lean (Tendsto, atTop)

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Foundational definitions: the **two-set representation function** $r_{A,B}(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A \times B : a+b=n\}|$, the **sumset** $A+B$, the **two-set basis** condition ($A+B$ covers all large integers), and the **counting function** $A(N) = |A \cap [1,N]|$.
sections.mathContext: $r_{A,B}(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A \times B : a + b = n\}|$; basis iff $(A+B)^c$ finite; $A(N) = |A \cap [1,N]|$.

sections.title: Asymptotic Density Condition
sections.summary: The key condition $a_n/b_n \to 1$ expressed via counting functions: $|A \cap [1,N]| / |B \cap [1,N]| \to 1$. This forces the two sets to have asymptotically equal enumerations.

sections.title: Basis Definition Equivalence
sections.summary: **Proved**: The two definitions of two-set basis are equivalent: $\exists N_0, \forall n \geq N_0, n \in A+B$ iff $(A+B)^c$ is finite.
sections.mathContext: $\exists N_0\,\forall n \geq N_0\,(n \in A+B) \iff (A+B)^c \text{ finite}$. Proved via sup of the finite complement.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Four proved structural results: (1) pairs summing to $n$ form a finite set; (2) $n \in A+B \Rightarrow r_{A,B}(n) \geq 1$; (3) monotonicity in both sets; (4) $r_{A,B}(n) = 0$ when $n < \min(A) + \min(B)$.
sections.mathContext: Finiteness, positivity, monotonicity, and vanishing for small $n$ — all proved from definitions.

sections.title: The Main Conjecture
sections.summary: **Erdős–Sárközy Conjecture**: If $A, B$ infinite with $a_n/b_n \to 1$ and $A+B$ is a basis, then $\forall k, \exists n: r_{A,B}(n) > k$. Stated as axiom (OPEN problem).

sections.title: Connection to Erdős–Turán (Problem #28)
sections.summary: **Proved**: When $A = B$, the ratio condition $a_n/a_n = 1$ is trivially satisfied, so Problem #1145 implies Problem #28. The proof constructs an eventually-equal-to-1 sequence using the infinitude of $A$.
sections.mathContext: $A = B \Rightarrow a_n/b_n = 1$, so #1145 specializes to the Erdős–Turán conjecture. Corollary: `erdos_1145_implies_28`.

sections.title: Necessity via Ruzsa's Counterexample
sections.summary: **Proved** (from axiomatized Ruzsa properties): The ratio condition $a_n/b_n \to 1$ is **necessary**. Ruzsa's binary digit construction gives $A, B$ with $A+B = \mathbb{N}$ but $r_{A,B}(n) = 1$ for all $n \geq 1$, and $a_n/b_n \to 1/2 \neq 1$.
sections.mathContext: Ruzsa: $A$ = even binary positions, $B$ = odd positions. Unique representations, bounded $r = 1$, $a_n/b_n \to 1/2$.

sections.title: Structural Results
sections.summary: **Proved**: (1) Symmetry: $r_{A,B}(n) = r_{B,A}(n)$ via a bijection $(a,b) \mapsto (b,a)$. (2) Vanishing: $r_{A,B}(n) = 0$ for $n > 2N$ when $A, B \subseteq [0,N]$.
sections.mathContext: Commutativity via pair-swap bijection; large-$n$ vanishing by bound on components.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Sárközy formulated this conjecture in their 1986 paper 'Problems and results on additive properties of general sequences, II' (Acta Math. Hungarica 48, 201–211), extending the classical Erdős–Turán conjecture (1941) from single-set bases to two-set bases. The original Erdős–Turán conjecture (Problem #28) asks whether r_{A,A}(n) must be unbounded when A + A covers all large integers — a question that remains open and carries a $500 Erdős prize. Problem #1145 generalizes this to distinct sets A, B with the crucial constraint that their enumerations grow at the same rate (aₙ/bₙ → 1). The necessity of this ratio condition was established by Imre Ruzsa, who solved the related Problem #331 by constructing sets A, B using binary digit interleaving where A + B = ℕ but every integer has exactly one representation (r = 1 everywhere). Partial progress includes the work of Grekos, Haddad, Helou, and Pihko, who showed that r_{A,B}(n) ≥ 6 infinitely often under the conjecture's hypotheses. The problem appears in Varga's 1999 collection [Va99, 1.17] and remains completely open as of 2026.
overview.problemStatement: Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\}$ and $B = \{b_1 < b_2 < \cdots\}$ be infinite sets of positive integers with $a_n/b_n \to 1$. If $A + B$ contains all sufficiently large integers, must $\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_{A,B}(n) = \infty$?
overview.text: The Erdős–Sárközy conjecture generalizes the famous Erdős–Turán conjecture from A + A to A + B, requiring that the two sets grow at the same rate.
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize the two-set representation function, state the conjecture as an axiom, and prove: (1) this implies the Erdős–Turán conjecture when A = B; (2) the ratio condition is necessary via Ruzsa's counterexample; (3) basic structural properties (symmetry, monotonicity, positivity, vanishing).
keyInsights: **Generalizes Erdős–Turán**: Setting A = B recovers Problem #28, proved as `erdos_1145_implies_28` — making this conjecture strictly stronger than the $500 Erdős prize problem
**Ratio condition is necessary**: Without aₙ/bₙ → 1, Ruzsa gives A + B = ℕ with r = 1 everywhere, proved as `ratio_condition_necessary`
**Ruzsa's binary digit construction**: Interleaving even- and odd-position binary digits creates sets where every sum has a unique representation, demonstrating the conjecture is optimally sharp
**Symmetry of representations**: r_{A,B}(n) = r_{B,A}(n) via explicit pair-swap bijection — the conjecture is invariant under swapping A and B

**Average vs pointwise growth**: The axiomatized average-representation result shows the average of r_{A,B}(n) diverges when both sets have density ≫ √N, but this does not directly imply the pointwise lim sup = ∞ required by the conjecture — highlighting the gap between average and extremal behavior

conclusion.summary: This formalization establishes the Erdős–Sárközy conjecture in Lean 4, connecting it to both the Erdős–Turán conjecture (Problem #28) as a special case and to Ruzsa's counterexample (Problem #331) showing the ratio condition is necessary. All 10 theorems are proved without sorry; the open conjecture and known results are axiomatized.
conclusion.implications: A proof of this conjecture would simultaneously resolve the Erdős–Turán conjecture ($500 bounty), since it is strictly stronger. The formalization makes precise exactly what condition distinguishes the true conjecture from its false generalization.
openQuestions: Can the asymptotic ratio condition aₙ/bₙ → 1 be weakened while preserving the conjecture?
Does the conjecture hold for A + B covering a positive density subset (not necessarily all large integers)?
What is the relationship between the growth rates of A and B and the growth rate of r_{A,B}(n)?

crossReferences.description: Problem #1145 generalizes #28: setting A = B recovers the Erdős–Turán conjecture. The implication is proved as erdos_1145_implies_28.
Problem #331 (disproved by Ruzsa) provides the counterexample showing the ratio condition aₙ/bₙ → 1 is necessary in Problem #1145.
